name: Vault notes and the human view
summary: The operator's Markdown vault: writing notes safely, write sessions, the rendered human view, vault scope and several vaults.

features.name: Vault note writing
features.summary: Creates, updates, appends, renames, moves and archives vault notes atomically, alone or in validated batches.
capabilities: Creates a note with frontmatter and body by temp-file write and rename; an existing target is refused or kept.
Merges frontmatter keys or replaces the body of a note, or appends Markdown text; a missing target is refused.
Refuses paths that traverse, enter `Brain/`, are out of scope or outside `write_binding.path_prefixes` when set.
Applies create, update, append, apply-evidence and log-line ops as one batch, validating all before any write.
Renames, moves, archives or deletes a note, or moves and renames a folder; dry run unless applied.
Rewrites inbound `[[wikilinks]]` after a move to the shortest spelling that still resolves
Writes a stub note for an unresolved wikilink target that links back to its sources (`scaffold-stub`)
limits: A fault during a batch's commit phase (a full disk) is not rolled back across files; each file write is atomic.
The write binding is a path boundary over caller-named paths, not a security boundary: it reads no identity.
After a move, search can return old paths until the claimed detached index refresh lands.
Deleting a user note needs an explicit confirm, since no archive covers it.

features.name: Agent write sessions
features.summary: A prompt, validate and approve cycle for model-written artifacts and decision panels, independent of the provider.
capabilities: Opens a session that returns a generation prompt with schema hints and collision data for an occupied target.
Validates a submitted artifact (256 KiB cap, target policy) and commits it atomically only when clean.
Returns machine-readable errors and a correction prompt for a failed submit
Writes by intent: create never overwrites, overwrite replaces, merge appends a session-stamped section.
Parks a validated artifact for an operator approve or abandon when opened with `require_review`.
Runs a decision panel: one step per persona lens (built-in or curated), then a synthesis note at the target.
Appends one `write-session` audit event per terminal transition.
limits: Generates no content: every byte comes from the calling agent's model.
Under `Brain/` it commits only to the page lanes, `Brain/decisions/panels/` and `Brain/notes/`.
Expiry is checked on read; no background timer sweeps sessions.
A session ends as failed after 3 attempts or 24 hours by default

features.name: Human view
features.summary: Renders plain Markdown pages of rules, history, decisions and topics; editing a page records a human correction.
capabilities: Renders `about-me.md`, weekly history, `decisions.md`, topic, report and source pages (default `o2b-memory/`).
Renders on one device only, the view writer (`view writer`)
Spots a human edit against the writer's own renders and three-way merges it, the user winning, into records.
Turns a reworded or deleted rule line of `about-me.md` into a human preference change or retirement.
Reads sync-tool conflict copies of a page as edits and removes them
Re-renders on the view writer at session start at most hourly (`view-render` hook) and after each dream pass.
Keeps replaced page versions as blobs and lists or prints them for 30 days (`view recover <page>`).
Writes generated headings in the `view.language` language, else English; quoted text stays as written.
limits: Renders from the shared partition only: a private preference or topic never appears on a page.
Needs a brain store and a device id; without them nothing renders.
Deleting a page retires nothing: a missing or empty page is rendered again.

features.name: Vault scope and layout
features.summary: Which vault paths are read, ignored or indexed, the folder role map, one-path inspection and a page listing.
capabilities: Puts a path in scope when no `vault.ignore_paths` rule matches and any declared `vault.include_paths` covers it.
Ignores `.git`, `node_modules`, `.obsidian`, `.trash`, `.stversions`, snapshots and its own folders by default.
Keeps lane-owned paths (exact state, pending review) out of the search index through one admission predicate.
Reports inclusion counts and excluded directories per rule, as the index would see them (`vault status`).
Gives two verdicts for one path, vault scope and write binding, naming the list that decided (`vault inspect`).
Prints `{{role}}` tokens (inbox, projects, areas) resolved to folders from `vault_map.document` (`vault map`).
Reads user notes for inline scans only under `notes.read_paths`, which is empty by default.
Lists the vault pages in scope by title substring (`second_brain_query`)
limits: The scope, include and read-path keys are operator-only: `brain_settings` refuses them to agents.
The vault map covers user content folders only, not the fixed `Brain/` layout.

features.name: Vault profiles and project links
features.summary: Named vault profiles, project directories linked to their vault, and other vaults read as recall sources.
capabilities: Keeps named vault profiles in `profiles.json` beside the config, one of them active
Resolves the vault from `VAULT_DIR`, the nearest `.o2b-vault.json` pointer, the active profile, then the config.
Links a project directory to its vault by a pointer file and a `projects.json` registry (`brain project link`).
Lists, checks and removes project links from the registry without scanning the filesystem (`brain project`).
Attaches other vaults as read-only recall sources, kept per owning vault (`brain source add|list|remove`).
Searches the active vault, profile vaults, read sources and the shared namespace with origin labels.
Activates a profile from MCP (`brain_switch_vault`); the change applies at the next server launch.
limits: A recall source is only read: no write and no index build happens inside it.
The profile, project and source registries live beside each machine's config file and are not synced.
A running MCP server keeps the vault it resolved at launch.
